also_covered_by.summary: Mozilla security advisory, impact high.

also_covered_by.title: Firefox 161: Free VPN now works on a per-site basis
also_covered_by.summary: Firefox 161 is here: Its built-in VPN now has rules for individual websites. A new shortcut also clears browser data.

also_covered_by.title: Firefox 161 Released: Fire Button Rolling Out to Regular Desktop Windows, VPN Gains Per-Site Controls
also_covered_by.summary: Mozilla is gradually bringing the Fire button for clearing selected browsing data to regular desktop windows in Firefox 161. The desktop browser's built-in VPN can now be enabled or disabled for individual sites regardless of its global setting.

items.title: Stalwart 1.2.0 lets Outlook keep working after an Exchange move
items.summary: Stalwart is an open-source mail server for organizations that want to host email themselves. Version 1.2.0 adds Exchange client protocols, letting users keep Outlook while their mailboxes move to Stalwart. The new compatibility is included in the free Community edition. Source

also_covered_by.title: Stalwart 1.2.0 Gains Exchange Compatibility, Offering a Migration Path That Keeps Classic Outlook
also_covered_by.summary: Open-source mail server Stalwart 1.2.0 now supports communication protocols used by Microsoft Exchange. Organizations can consider migrating their servers while continuing to use classic Outlook for email, calendars, and contacts.

items.title: OpenAI, Cisco Unveil Open Source Tool to Shield Unpatched Linux Systems
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco’s Shirudo uses AI-generated shields to block Linux exploits while patches are prepared, but it’s not yet production-ready.

also_covered_by.title: Cisco and OpenAI Launch Shirudo for Linux Runtime Security
also_covered_by.summary: Cisco and OpenAI’s Shirudo aims to protect running Linux systems while teams roll out patches. See what IT teams can test and what they need to run it.

also_covered_by.title: OpenAI and Cisco Unveil AI-Assisted Linux Security Tool to Block Exploits Before Patching
also_covered_by.summary: OpenAI and Cisco have teamed up to launch Shirudo (meaning "shield" in Japanese), an open-source Linux runtime that allows artificial intelligence (AI) agents to defend systems without downtime.

also_covered_by.title: OpenAI and Cisco Release Shirudo, Adding Temporary Protection Without Stopping Linux
also_covered_by.summary: OpenAI and Cisco have released Shirudo, an open-source platform that adds temporary protections to running Linux systems. AI generates safeguards and operators approve their deployment; in a Java4Shell test, it blocked an attack without restarting the service.

also_covered_by.title: Linux patches can take weeks, and OpenAI and Cisco built Shirudo to help in the meantime
also_covered_by.summary: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source tool that puts temporary protections on running Linux systems while their owners work on a patch. also_covered_by.title: OpenAI and Cisco Release Open-Source Tool to Shield Unpatched Linux Systems
also_covered_by.summary: OpenAI and Cisco’s Shirudo helps Linux users block exploitation of known vulnerabilities on live systems, buying time for patching without requiring a restart

also_covered_by.title: Cisco and OpenAI Unveil Shirudo, an eBPF-Based Linux Security Platform
also_covered_by.summary: Shirudo is a new open-source Linux security platform from Cisco and OpenAI that combines eBPF and AI-assisted vulnerability mitigation.

also_covered_by.title: Shirudo: OpenAI and Cisco unveil AI-powered shield for Linux servers
also_covered_by.summary: Shirudo lets AI agents develop temporary protections designed to safeguard Linux systems until security patches are installed.

also_covered_by.title: New Shirudo tool uses AI to shield unpatched Linux systems from exploits
also_covered_by.summary: OpenAI and Cisco launched an open-source Linux security tool named Shirudo that deploys temporary runtime protections to block vulnerability exploitation while administrators prepare and roll out patches, without restarting services. [...]

also_covered_by.title: Astelia’s autonomous network mitigation blocks AI-driven exploits without a patch
also_covered_by.summary: Exposure management company Astelia Inc. today announced the launch of autonomous network mitigation, a new capability that allows organizations to block artificial intelligence-driven exploits at the network level, even when a patch isn’t available or can’t be applied.

also_covered_by.title: OpenAI, Cisco debut tool that lets AI agents safely block vulnerability exploitation
also_covered_by.summary: The new framework can provide temporary protection while organizations test patches.

also_covered_by.title: Cisco and OpenAI dispatch AI agents to shield vulnerable systems before permanent patches arrive
also_covered_by.summary: Autonomous AI agents are rapidly and dramatically transforming the cybersecurity landscape for both defenders and adversaries. In hopes of giving security teams a head start and pitting machine against machine, Cisco and OpenAI have released a new open source project, dubbed Shirudo (Japanese for “shield”).
